syllabusTopics: Nuclear density; mass number; atomic number
Mass defect, packing fraction, binding energy per nucleon
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9 (extra unit card). Exam bank: decay constant (2024), mass defect (2023), 8-day half-life (2023).

card.title: Exam bank — every board question on nuclear physics

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Three questions: decay constant plus half-life relation (2024), mass defect vs binding energy (2023), 8-day half-life fraction after 24 days (2023: 1/8 remains). Decay is statistical (N = N0 e^-lambda t); binding energy per nucleon peaks at iron-56, so fission splits heavies and fusion joins lights downhill.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: N = N0 e^(-lambda t) · A = lambda N · T-half = ln2/lambda = 0.693/lambda · E = m c2, 1 u = 931.5 MeV · remaining after n lives = (1/2)^n

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Exponential law needs large N (statistics meaningless for atoms few). Half-life relation is exact only for single-decay chains. Binding comparisons use per-NUCLEON values (totals mislead across masses). E = mc2 prices conversion, never reaction rates.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 24 days at T-half 8 days = 3 lives, so 1/8 remains and activity falls identically. Mass defect means assembled nuclei weigh LESS than parts (missing mass became binding). Pair production needs 1.02 MeV threshold; annihilation returns 2 gamma.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): n = 24/8 = 3 half-lives, remaining (1/2)3 = 1/8; activity A = lambda N drops by the same factor. NEB 2023 (3): mass defect (parts minus nucleus) times c2 equals binding energy. NEB 2024 (2): lambda defined via dN/dt = -lambda N with T-half = 0.693/lambda.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: half-life predicts populations, never single atoms; linear instead of exponential decay assumed; mass defect sign flipped. Liquid-drop trends are semi-empirical (shell structure adds fine print).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: dN/dt = -lambda N separates and integrates to exponential form; halving gives T-half. Binding from weighing parts vs nucleus times c2; iron-56 maximum explains why both fission and fusion release energy.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Half-life: count lives n = t/T, remaining (1/2)^n. 'Define decay constant' means dN/dt relation plus T-half link. Binding: defect, times 931.5, divide by A.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (2): decay constant + half-life relation. NEB 2023 (3): mass defect vs binding energy. NEB 2023 (3): 8-day half-life, fraction after 24 days + activity.
